evidenceBasis.sourceIdentity: Root verified all 57 source-file SHA-256 values against snapshot-01 before delta edits began.

p0p1.scope: No P0/P1 issue is substantiated by these three sealed reports and the source paths sampled. This does not claim coverage beyond their scope.

decisions.decision: Accept the code-path observation; do not require per-page manifest polling under the stated user scope. Close through precise documentation and explicit fixed-snapshot semantics, conditional on the README delta making the retry/resume boundary unambiguous.
basis: The supplied user requirement is to queue and download one Hitomi gallery; it does not require tracking revisions while an uninterrupted run is in progress.

In the immutable snapshot, refreshGalleryManifest compares title, total, ordered image hashes and names when called. Retry/start/recovery paths request revalidation, while successful page completion calls startGalleryPage with revalidate=false and advances from the persisted image snapshot (engine.ts around lines 251-350, 395-459, 590-596, 1037-1041).

README at the base commit describes revalidation in the retry sentence; its nearby content-change stop wording can be read more broadly than the implementation. The distinction should be stated directly: changes are detected when a retry/resume revalidates, while an uninterrupted run finishes from the original saved snapshot.

Reloading a manifest before every page would add up to 2,000 repeated full-list requests and still cannot guarantee that the source will not change after the check but before a later image request. A single persisted snapshot gives a coherent same-gallery version boundary. If old image URLs stop working, the page can fail and the retry-time revalidation will detect a changed manifest.
decisions.risk: During an uninterrupted run, newly published manifest changes are not noticed immediately; the queue may continue requesting the original snapshot's hashes. That behavior is coherent with the requested single-gallery download, but would violate a separate explicit requirement to stop on any mid-run source revision.
minimumClosure: Clarify README wording so the stop-on-change statement explicitly applies when retry/resume revalidates the saved snapshot; state that uninterrupted runs use the original snapshot through completion.
Keep the existing retry/resume changed-manifest guard and its regression evidence; do not describe this as live revision monitoring.
If the product owner later requires immediate mid-run revision detection, treat that as a changed requirement and assess a bounded policy; do not silently implement per-page full-manifest polling.

decisions.decision: Confirm. The sealed report's source path shows that an unknown total renders only a bare completed-page number, with a generic progress accessible name; this is a real ambiguity across the listed locales.
basis: critic-ux reports galleryPageProgress returning String(done) when total is absent and aria-label containing only the gallery name for an indeterminate progress element.
The planned localized page unit/unknown-total wording and ARIA name directly address both visual and screen-reader ambiguity.
minimumClosure: Add translated unknown-total text with an explicit page unit for English, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese, and include completed count plus unknown total in the accessible name.
Update focused UI assertions to cover the unknown-total branch and all supported locale copy paths; preserve determinate-total behavior.
Record the exact source/test delta and fresh focused-test result separately from snapshot-01 evidence.

decisions.decision: Confirm. The runner sorts actualHashes in place for set comparison, then reports those sorted values against the original download order. This invalidates filename-to-digest report pairing and can let a page-order mismatch pass; it does not prove a production ordering defect.
basis: The immutable runner at tests/browser/gallery.mjs around lines 647-662 sorts actualHashes and later indexes it using own.indexOf(download).
The sealed report provides a concrete first/second fixture digest swap; the engine's completed-index selection path alone does not establish a product ordering regression.

The cited Katfile run is failed/preparing with zero fixture requests and cannot be attributed to product or environment. The earlier 23-pass run is a different background build hash and is not evidence for this snapshot.
minimumClosure: Fix the runner to preserve each file's digest with its corresponding download record; sort a copy only if an unordered-set assertion is still useful.
Run a fresh gallery browser acceptance against the identified delta build and verify each numbered filename's digest against the fixture metadata index, not just the digest set.

Keep the failed Katfile run labeled inconclusive. Do not promote the older 23-pass run into a pass claim for the delta build; obtain a new same-build Katfile run if that regression evidence is required.

blockedGalleryNotificationRoute.decision: Accept with a narrow routing predicate.
blockedGalleryNotificationRoute.basis: In snapshot-01, notification clicks for verify/block IDs both issue focus. focusItem opens item.sourceUrl if it cannot focus a matching tab; for a blocked gallery with an ambiguous download handoff, the notification should take the user to Chrome downloads history so they can reconcile the transfer.
blockedGalleryNotificationRoute.boundary: Route to downloads history only for a blocked gallery with download intent (action.kind === download or a persisted downloadId). Keep ordinary metadata/source focus behavior, and do not route every blocked gallery indiscriminately.
minimumClosure: Add a focused adapter/engine-level assertion for the blocked gallery download-intent route.
Add a contrast assertion that a gallery blocked during metadata/source processing retains source focus behavior, plus existing Katfile verification/source focus behavior.
Confirm notification click IDs still resolve to the intended queue item after restart; label any browser/UI verification as synthetic or unperformed according to the actual evidence.

chairProposal.katfileDiagnostic: The latest failed/preparing/zero-request run is inconclusive. It must remain a diagnostic record, not a product failure attribution or pass. The older 23-pass run belongs to a different build and must remain separate.

limits: This initial arbitration relies on the three named sealed critic reports and snapshot-01 only; it does not claim the delta is implemented or verified.
No real Hitomi image transfer, live source-revision timing, personal Chrome flow, or delta build was tested.
Synthetic gallery evidence and older/different-build Katfile evidence remain separate from any new delta build/run evidence.
rootClosureChecklist: Provide snapshot-02 or an equivalent immutable delta identity with source hashes for the revised documentation, localized unknown-total UI, notification routing, and browser runner.
Provide changed-file inventory and fresh focused unit/UI test results for unknown totals and narrowly scoped notification routing.
Provide a new gallery browser report whose per-file digest pairs are correct and whose tested build identity matches the delta.
If claiming Katfile coexistence for the delta, provide a fresh same-build Katfile run; otherwise retain Review/inconclusive wording.
Keep real-site behavior unverified unless separately observed; do not merge synthetic run claims with real-site claims.
